title: Corporate Learning and Skills Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Employer learning, skills development, authoring, content and training-procurement alternatives, with Studytube as the reference company.
inclusionLogic: Direct enterprise and midmarket learning platforms compete for the employer academy decision.
HR-suite learning is adjacent because existing HR contracts and integration strategy can influence the purchase.
Content subscriptions compete for learning spend and may also supply a retained LMS.
Training-provider platforms matter to supplier operations without being equivalent to employer academies.
Keeping spreadsheets, a legacy LMS and separately purchased training is an unquantified workflow substitute; it is not treated as a company.
notes: All descriptions are analytical comparisons from official product pages, not verified feature-by-feature procurement evaluations.
Category labels distinguish broad enterprise, regional, challenger and specialized offers; global_leader is not a measured market-share ranking.
Primary regions are coarse comparison context based on reviewed office/product coverage, not a geographic revenue breakdown.
Stats retain their published labels and scope. Organizations, teams, training organizations, languages and countries are not comparable measures and must not be ranked together.
No revenue, ARR, valuation, profitability or market-share estimate is invented. Empty businessStats means no suitable comparable metric was retained.
Publication dates are unknown for undated webpages. Access dates are observations, not measurement periods.
360Learning headquarters remain unverified; Moodle location context is historical and explicitly labeled. Neither affects the product comparison.
The Moodle Workplace URL was available in the official search index but direct retrieval failed during research; verify its current page and terms during procurement.

players.name: Studytube
players.description: Reference company: brings employer learning administration, skills development, authoring and content together, with external-training intermediation where enabled. Its modeled advantage is the coherence of those workflows; this is a strategy hypothesis rather than a market-share claim. Relationship: reference.

businessStats.scope: Studytube public company/product claim, not paying-customer or active-user verification

players.name: Docebo
players.description: Enterprise learning and skills platform spanning LMS, learner experience, authoring and multiple audiences. Direct comparison for employers consolidating learning technology; breadth and enterprise integration are the relevant purchase dimensions. Relationship: direct.

businessStats.scope: Company-wide organizations described on the homepage; not a corporate-LMS-only count

players.name: 360Learning
players.hq: Not verified in the reviewed primary sources
players.description: Collaborative learning platform emphasizing expert-created content, AI-assisted authoring, skills and enterprise integrations. Direct comparison for employers seeking participation from internal subject matter experts and scalable learning administration. Relationship: direct.

businessStats.scope: Reported teams; not normalized to customer organizations or paying accounts

players.name: Cornerstone
players.description: Workforce platform covering learning, skills, talent development and content. A direct or suite-led alternative for large employers whose learning choice is tied to broader workforce systems and enterprise procurement. Relationship: direct and suite-adjacent.

businessStats.scope: Company-wide geographic footprint; not customer count, market share or LMS-only reach

players.name: aNewSpring
players.description: Platform for training organizations combining authoring, learning delivery, learner experience and commerce. Particularly relevant to the training-provider persona; it can compete with or complement the employer's learning platform rather than substituting for every employer workflow. Relationship: provider-focused adjacent.

businessStats.scope: Training-organization customer claim; not employer-academy customers

players.name: GoodHabitz
players.description: Workplace content for human and digital skills, delivered through its platform or an employer's existing LMS. A content-budget substitute and possible complement, especially where the employer keeps its existing learning administration stack. Relationship: content substitute and complement.

businessStats.scope: Language availability claim; not catalog size, employer count or learning outcomes

players.name: SAP SuccessFactors Learning
players.description: Corporate learning system available standalone or within the SuccessFactors HCM suite. A suite-adjacent competitor when employers prioritize HR integration, compliance learning and an existing enterprise vendor relationship. Relationship: suite-adjacent.

players.name: Moodle Workplace
players.hq: Perth, Australia; Barcelona, Spain (historical company description; current headquarters not reverified)
players.description: Configurable enterprise learning platform supported through Moodle's service and partner ecosystem. A platform substitute for employers preferring implementation flexibility and partner delivery; total operating effort must be evaluated separately from license terms. Relationship: configurable-platform substitute.

players.name: LearnUpon
players.description: Learning platform with employee learning, multiple portals, authoring, skills and reporting capabilities. A direct comparison for an employer needing audience separation and learning operations, with customer education providing adjacent scope. Relationship: direct.
